page.description: Lakka editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A lightweight retro-gaming system built on LibreELEC and RetroArch: write one image to a stick, boot it, and play with a gamepad from a TV-style interface.
pros: Turns a spare PC into a retro console in one write.
RetroArch with hundreds of cores, configured in one interface.
Four x86 images, so AMD, Intel and nVidia GPUs are covered.
Small download compared with a full desktop.
cons: An appliance, not a desktop: the publisher does not support virtualisation or dual boot.
It may not work on a given PC's hardware.
USB images only: there are no CD or DVD images.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Lakka; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the .img.gz to a USB stick or SD card with an image writer; writing erases the whole device. The system then runs from, or installs to, that device.
